title: Tomato Breeds: From Cherokee Purple to San Marzano
imageHint: A colorful array of different tomato varieties - red, purple, yellow, and green in various shapes and sizes
description: From ancient Andean varieties to modern hybrids, tomato breeding combines centuries of agricultural tradition with cutting-edge genetics to create varieties optimized for flavor, disease resistance, and growing conditions.

questions.question: What is the difference between heirloom and hybrid tomato varieties?
questions.answer: Heirloom varieties breed true to type
acceptableAnswers: Heirloom varieties breed true to type
questions.explanation: Heirloom tomatoes are open-pollinated varieties that breed true to type, meaning seeds saved from the fruit will produce plants identical to the parent, unlike hybrids.

questions.question: Which Italian heirloom tomato variety is considered the gold standard for making authentic San Marzano sauce?
questions.explanation: San Marzano tomatoes, grown in the volcanic soil near Naples, Italy, are prized for their sweet flavor, low acidity, and thick flesh, making them ideal for traditional Italian sauces.

questions.question: What gives the Cherokee Purple heirloom tomato its distinctive dark coloration?
questions.explanation: Cherokee Purple tomatoes get their distinctive dark purple-red color from high levels of anthocyanins, the same antioxidant compounds that color blueberries and red wine.

questions.question: What breeding technique creates F1 hybrid tomatoes that often show improved vigor but don't breed true from saved seeds?
questions.explanation: F1 hybrids are created through controlled cross-pollination of two different parent varieties, resulting in uniform plants with hybrid vigor, but seeds won't reproduce the same characteristics.

questions.question: Which determinate tomato characteristic makes them preferred for commercial canning operations?
questions.explanation: Determinate tomatoes ripen their entire crop over a 2-3 week period, allowing for efficient mechanical harvesting and processing, unlike indeterminate varieties that ripen continuously.
